newsitem.title: GERMANY: DG Bank 96 profit rises 66 pct.
newsitem.headline: DG Bank 96 profit rises 66 pct.

text.p: DG Bank, the German co-operative bank, said on Thursday it increased its operating profit by 66 percent in 1996 and plans to pay an unchanged dividend.

Group operating profit after risk provisions rose to 868.7 million marks ($506.9 million) from 523.9 million, aided by strong gains in interest income and a 47.1 percent drop in risk provisions to 165.2 million, the bank said.
DG Bank paid a dividend of 2.75 percent after tax for 1995, the first full payout for five years.
"1996 was characterised by solid growth and pleasingly dynamic earnings," DG Bank chief executive Bernd Thiemann said in a statement.
DG Bank has emerged from a lengthy restructuring after write-offs on a large and controversial bond deal with French banks caused a sharp drop in profits in 1991.
The bank said group net interest income jumped 19.1 percent to 3.3 billion marks last year.
Net commission income fell 16.4 percent to 240.5 million marks due to accounting changes which will however lead to a compensating boost to commission income in coming years, the bank said.
Net income from financial transactions rose by 2.5 percent to 187 million marks. Administration costs rose 4.4 percent to 1.19 billion marks.
The group's balance sheet total grew 13.8 percent to 331.3 billion marks.
